---
title: Shape Marginalization by Spectral Panels
---

This page describes [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral]], which computes the marginal
of the observed ellipticity over the intrinsic one,
$$
P(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} \mid g) = \int_{|\chi_I|<1} \mathrm{d}^2\chi_I\,
P_\mathrm{pop}(\chi_I)\, N_2\big(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - f_g(\chi_I);\,
\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2\big) ,
\tag{1}
$$
where $P_\mathrm{pop}$ is the isotropic density of the intrinsic ellipticity $\chi_I$,
$f_g$ the shear map of the ellipticity convention, $g$ the reduced shear and $N_2$ the
isotropic two-dimensional Gaussian of variance $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2$ per component. The
integral is computed by [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]], described in
[Spectral Integration on a Disk](../../../ncm/algebra/spectral_polar.qmd), in the polar
coordinates of a variable of integration $\zeta$ that depends on the ellipticity
convention, defined in [The Variable of Integration](#the-variable-of-integration).

## The Shear Modulus

The integral depends on the shear through its modulus and through the angle between $g$
and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$. Three cases are separated before anything is integrated.

- $|g| = 1$: every point of the open disk maps to $g$, and
  $P = N_2 (\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - g; \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2)$.
- $|g| > 1$: for an isotropic population the integral equals the one at $g / |g|^2$, which
  has the same phase and modulus $1 / |g|$. That shear replaces $g$.
- The frame is rotated by the phase $\varphi$ of $g$: with $t \equiv |g| < 1$ and
  $\epsilon \equiv \epsilon_\mathrm{obs} e^{-i \varphi}$, Eq. (1) is the same integral
  with the real shear $t$ and the observed ellipticity $\epsilon$, since
  $f_g (\chi) = e^{i \varphi} f_t (\chi e^{-i \varphi})$ and $P_\mathrm{pop}$ is isotropic.

## The Variable of Integration

For `NC_GALAXY_WL_OBS_ELLIP_CONV_TRACE_DET` the integral is computed in $\chi_I$. For
`NC_GALAXY_WL_OBS_ELLIP_CONV_TRACE` it is computed in the trace--determinant ellipticity
of the same intrinsic shape. This section defines that variable, writes Eq. (1) in it and
states why it is used.

### The two ellipticities of one shape

A shape with axis ratio $q \le 1$ and orientation $\varphi_s$ has the trace ellipticity
$\chi_s$ and the trace--determinant ellipticity $\epsilon_s$ of
[Galaxy Shapes and Ellipticity Frames](wl_ellipticity.qmd),
$$
\chi_s = \frac{1 - q^2}{1 + q^2} \, e^{2 i \varphi_s} ,
\qquad
\epsilon_s = \frac{1 - q}{1 + q} \, e^{2 i \varphi_s} .
$$
They have the same phase, and eliminating $q$ gives $\chi_s = T (\epsilon_s)$ with
$$
T (w) \equiv \frac{2 w}{1 + |w|^2} ,
\qquad
T^{-1} (w) = \frac{w}{1 + \sqrt{1 - |w|^2}} .
$$
The map $T$ takes the open unit disk onto itself and the unit circle onto itself. For the
moduli, $|T (w)| = u (|w|)$ with
$$
u (r) \equiv \frac{2 r}{1 + r^2} ,
\qquad
1 - u (r) = \frac{(1 - r)^2}{1 + r^2} ,
\qquad
u' (r) = \frac{2 (1 - r^2)}{(1 + r^2)^2} .
\tag{2}
$$

### The shear map

The shear acts on the shape, so the maps of the two conventions are one operation written
in the two ellipticities. With $t < 1$ real, the trace--determinant map is
$$
m_t (w) \equiv \frac{w + t}{1 + t w} ,
$$
and the trace map is
$$
f_t (w) = \frac{w + 2 t + t^2 \bar{w}}{1 + t^2 + 2 t \, \mathrm{Re} \, w}
= T \big( m_t (T^{-1} (w)) \big) .
\tag{3}
$$
The second equality was checked numerically on $10^4$ random pairs $(t, w)$ to
$2 \times 10^{-15}$. The class evaluates $m_t$ with
[[numcosmo|nc_wl_ellipticity_apply_shear_trace_det_real]] for both conventions.

### Eq. (1) in the trace--determinant ellipticity

For the trace convention the population is the density of $|\chi_I|$, normalized in
$\mathrm{d} |\chi_I|$, and it stays so. In the polar coordinates of $\chi_I$, with $\theta$
its angle, Eq. (1) is
$$
P = \int_0^{2 \pi} \!\! \int_0^1 \frac{P_\mathrm{pop} (|\chi_I|)}{2 \pi} \,
N_2 \big( \epsilon - f_t (\chi_I); \, \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2 \big) \,
\mathrm{d} |\chi_I| \, \mathrm{d}\theta .
$$
Every $\chi_I$ of the disk corresponds to one $\epsilon_I \equiv T^{-1} (\chi_I)$, the
trace--determinant ellipticity of the same shape. It has the angle $\theta$ of $\chi_I$,
and its modulus $r \equiv |\epsilon_I|$ satisfies $|\chi_I| = u (r)$. The integral over
$|\chi_I|$ is written as an integral over $r$,
$$
P_\mathrm{pop} (|\chi_I|) \, \mathrm{d} |\chi_I| = P_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) \, u' (r) \, \mathrm{d}r :
$$
the probability of an interval of $|\chi_I|$, written for the interval of $r$ that
corresponds to it. The product $P_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) \, u' (r)$ is the density of $r$
for the same population, not a population defined in $\epsilon_I$.

The population $P_\mathrm{pop}$ is written as its two end power laws times a function that
is finite at both ends,
$$
P_\mathrm{pop} (|\chi_I|) = |\chi_I|^{\alpha_o} (1 - |\chi_I|)^{\alpha_1} \, \hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (|\chi_I|) ,
$$
with $\alpha_o$ given by [[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_pop_exponent_at_origin]], $\alpha_1$
by [[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_pop_exponent_at_one]] and $\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop}$ by
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_pop_eval_p_reduced]]. With Eq. (2), the density of $r$ is
$$
P_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) \, u' (r) = r^{\alpha_o} (1 - r)^{2 \alpha_1 + 1} \, \hat{P}_\epsilon (r) ,
\qquad
\hat{P}_\epsilon (r) \equiv \frac{2^{\alpha_o + 1} (1 + r)}{(1 + r^2)^{\alpha_o + \alpha_1 + 2}} \,
\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) .
\tag{4}
$$
The three factors of the left side contribute as follows:
$u^{\alpha_o} = 2^{\alpha_o} r^{\alpha_o} (1 + r^2)^{-\alpha_o}$,
$(1 - u)^{\alpha_1} = (1 - r)^{2 \alpha_1} (1 + r^2)^{-\alpha_1}$ and
$u' = 2 (1 - r) (1 + r) (1 + r^2)^{-2}$. The exponent at $r = 1$ changes from $\alpha_1$
to $2 \alpha_1 + 1$, and $\hat{P}_\epsilon$ is finite at both ends. In the noise factor,
$f_t (\chi_I) = f_t (T (\epsilon_I)) = T (m_t (\epsilon_I))$ by Eq. (3): the outer $T$ converts
the sheared shape back to the trace ellipticity, in which it is observed. Eq. (1) becomes
$$
P = \int_0^{2 \pi} \!\! \int_0^1 r^{\alpha_o} (1 - r)^{2 \alpha_1 + 1} \,
\frac{\hat{P}_\epsilon (r)}{2 \pi} \,
N_2 \big( \epsilon - T (m_t (r e^{i \theta})); \, \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2 \big) \,
\mathrm{d}r \, \mathrm{d}\theta .
$$
Nothing is approximated: it is the integral above after the substitution
$\chi_I = T (\epsilon_I)$, the same number for every population and every $t$.

### Why this variable

Let $\delta \equiv 1 - t$. The two forms of the map are compared near $|g| = 1$, where
every point of the disk except a neighborhood of $-1$ maps close to $g$.

- In $\epsilon_I$: $m_t (\epsilon_I) - 1 = -\delta \, (1 - \epsilon_I) / (1 + t \epsilon_I)$.
  The denominator is zero at $\epsilon_I = -1 / t$, at the distance $\delta / t$ from the
  unit circle, so the map varies on the scale $\delta$ around $\epsilon_I = -1$, in $r$
  and in $\theta$.
- In $\chi_I = x + i y$:
  $f_t (\chi_I) = [(1 + t^2) x + 2 t + i (1 - t^2) y] / [\delta^2 + 2 t (1 + x)]$. The
  denominator changes by its own size when $1 + x$ changes by $\delta^2 / 2 t$, so the map
  varies on the scale $\delta^2$ in $r$ around $\chi_I = -1$ and on the scale $\delta$
  in $\theta$.
- The two statements are the same fact: by Eq. (2), the distance $\delta$ to the unit
  circle in $\epsilon_I$ is the distance $\delta^2 / 2$ in $\chi_I$.

The panels of [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]] halve until they resolve the scale of
the integrand, up to [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar:max-depth]]. At $\delta = 10^{-5}$
the scale is $10^{-5}$ in $\epsilon_I$ and $10^{-10}$ in $\chi_I$, where a radius also
keeps only six significant digits of $1 - r$ in double precision.

### The variable $\zeta$ for both conventions

In the sections below $\zeta = r e^{i \theta}$ is the variable of integration, $F_t$ the
map from $\zeta$ to the sheared ellipticity, and $r^{a} (1 - r)^{b} \hat{P}_\zeta (r)$ the
density of $r$:

| | $\zeta$ | $F_t (\zeta)$ | $a$ | $b$ | $\hat{P}_\zeta (r)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRACE_DET` | $\chi_I$ | $m_t (\zeta)$ | $\alpha_o$ | $\alpha_1$ | $\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (r)$ |
| `TRACE` | $T^{-1} (\chi_I)$ | $T (m_t (\zeta))$ | $\alpha_o$ | $2 \alpha_1 + 1$ | $\hat{P}_\epsilon (r)$ of Eq. (4) |

The truncated Gaussian populations have $\alpha_o = 1$ and $\alpha_1 = 0$, and the Beta
population $\alpha_o = \alpha - 1$ and $\alpha_1 = \beta - 1$ with a constant
$\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop}$.

## The Integral in Polar Coordinates

The density of $r$ is normalized in $\mathrm{d}r$, so the area density is that density
divided by $2 \pi r$, and Eq. (1) is
$$
P = e^{-d_0 / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2} \int_0^{2\pi} \!\! \int_0^1 r^{a} (1 - r)^{b} \, G (r, \theta) \, \mathrm{d}r \, \mathrm{d}\theta ,
\qquad
G (r, \theta) \equiv \frac{\hat{P}_\zeta (r)}{2 \pi} \,
\frac{e^{-(d (r, \theta) - d_0) / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2}}{2 \pi \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2} ,
\tag{5}
$$
with $d (r, \theta) \equiv |\epsilon - F_t (r e^{i \theta})|^2$ and $d_0$ an offset taken
out of the exponent so that $G$ stays in the double range. This is the integral of
[Spectral Integration on a Disk](../../../ncm/algebra/spectral_polar.qmd) with $R = 1$,
the exponents $a$ and $b$ of the table above and the function $G$.

## Locating the Peak

The panels are placed around the peak of the integrand, which is narrow when
$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ is small. The peak is searched on one ray.

- The center of the noise factor is $c \equiv F_t^{-1} (\epsilon_0)$, with
  $\epsilon_0 = \epsilon$ for $|\epsilon| < 1$ and otherwise the point of the unit circle
  in the direction of $\epsilon$, moved inside by $10^{-12}$. For `TRACE`,
  $F_t^{-1} = m_t^{-1} \circ T^{-1}$. The ray has the angle $\theta_0 \equiv \arg c$.
- $J_1$ and $J_2$ are the radial and the tangential stretch factors of $F_t^{-1}$ at
  $\epsilon_0$, by finite differences. The noise factor has the widths
  $\sigma_\mathrm{noise} J_1$ and $\sigma_\mathrm{noise} J_2$ around $c$.
- The function
  $$
  h (r) \equiv a \ln r + b \ln (1 - r) + \ln \hat{P}_\zeta (r) - \frac{d (r, \theta_0)}{2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2}
  $$
  is evaluated on a scan of the ray: 401 uniform radii, radii at $10^{-k}$ and
  $1 - 10^{-k}$ for $k = 2, \dots, 12$, and $|c|$ plus and minus multiples from $1/4$ to
  $25$ of the two widths. The radius $r_*$ is the maximum of $h$ by golden section between
  the neighbors of the best radius of the scan.
- $d_0$ is the smallest $d (r, \theta_0)$ of the scan.

The edges are those of [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_peak_edges]] for a peak at
$(r_*, \theta_0)$ with the radial half width
$L \equiv \sigma_\mathrm{noise} \min (J_1, J_2)$ and the angular half width $L / r_*$. They
cover the whole disk.

The scan places the panels and sets $d_0$. It does not decide what is integrated: every
panel is accepted by the test of [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]], and a panel where
$G$ is negligible is accepted on its starting grid by the absolute term of that test. A
peak placed wrongly changes the number of evaluations of $G$.

## Result and Errors

For $1 - t \ge 10^{-5}$ the class computes
$$
\ln P = \ln I - \frac{d_0}{2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2} ,
$$
with $I$ the integral of Eq. (5) from [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_integrate]] at
the relative tolerance `reltol` and absolute tolerance zero.
The function [[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_factor_eval_marginal]] returns $e^{\ln P}$. An
integral that fails with `NCM_SPECTRAL_POLAR_ERROR_MAX_DEPTH`, or a non-finite $\ln P$,
aborts with the population, $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$, $g$ and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ in
the message. For $1 - t < 10^{-5}$ the value is the one of the next section.

## Shears Next to $|g| = 1$

Let $\delta \equiv 1 - t$ and $\delta_s \equiv 10^{-5}$. By
[The Variable of Integration](#the-variable-of-integration) the integrand of Eq. (5)
varies on the scale $\delta$ around $\zeta = -1$, and a radius in double precision carries
$1 - r$ with an absolute error of $10^{-16}$. For $\delta < \delta_s$ the integral is not
computed at $t$. The marginal is written as a sum of two terms, $P = A (t) + B (t)$, and
the integrals are computed at $t_s \equiv 1 - \delta_s$.

### The second-order term $A$

Let $w \equiv m_t (\zeta)$ be the trace--determinant ellipticity after the shear, and
$\Phi (w) \equiv N_2 (\epsilon - C (w); \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2)$ the noise factor, with $C$
the identity for `TRACE_DET` and $C = T$ for `TRACE`. The function
$m_t (\zeta) - t = (1 - t^2) \, \zeta / (1 + t \zeta)$ is holomorphic in the disk and zero
at $\zeta = 0$, so for an isotropic population $w$ has the mean $t$ and the same variance
$s (t)$ in its two components, with no correlation:
$$
s (t) \equiv \frac{1}{2} \big\langle |w - t|^2 \big\rangle
= \frac{(1 - t^2)^2}{2} \int_0^1 r^{a} (1 - r)^{b} \, \hat{P}_\zeta (r) \,
\frac{r^2}{1 - t^2 r^2} \, \mathrm{d}r .
\tag{6}
$$
The expansion of $\Phi$ around $w = t$ to second order, averaged over the population, is
$$
A (t) \equiv \Phi (t) + \frac{s (t)}{2} \, \nabla^2 \Phi (t) .
\tag{7}
$$
With $D (w) \equiv |\epsilon - C (w)|^2$,
$\nabla^2 \Phi / \Phi = -\nabla^2 D / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2 + |\nabla D|^2 / 4 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^4$.
At $w = t$:

- `TRACE_DET`: $D = |\epsilon - t|^2$, $|\nabla D|^2 = 4 D$ and $\nabla^2 D = 4$.
- `TRACE`: with $q \equiv 1 + t^2$, $\Delta_1 \equiv \mathrm{Re} \, \epsilon - 2 t / q$ and
  $\Delta_2 \equiv \mathrm{Im} \, \epsilon$, $D = \Delta_1^2 + \Delta_2^2$,
  $\nabla D = \big( -4 \Delta_1 (1 - t^2) / q^2 , \, -4 \Delta_2 / q \big)$ and
  $\nabla^2 D = 8 (1 - t^2)^2 / q^4 + 8 / q^2 + 32 \, t \, \Delta_1 / q^3$.

The integral of Eq. (6) is computed by [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_integrate]] in
$v \equiv 1 - r$, in which $1 - t^2 r^2 = (\delta + t v) (1 + t r)$ is formed without a
difference of numbers close to 1, with the radial edges of
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_peak_edges]] for a peak at $v = 0$ of half width
$\delta$. The term $A$ is accurate when the next order is small, which requires
$\delta \, |\epsilon - g| \ll \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2$.

### The term $B$ of the neighborhood of $\zeta = -1$

The remainder $B \equiv P - A$ is what the expansion of Eq. (7) does not contain: the
neighborhood of $\zeta = -1$ of size $\delta$, whose image by $m_t$ is the whole disk and
not a neighborhood of $t$. In the variable $z \equiv (1 + w) / (1 - w)$ the map $m_t$ is
the multiplication by
$$
\lambda \equiv \frac{1 + t}{1 - t} ,
$$
and the expansion of the density of $\zeta$ around $\zeta = -1$ gives
$$
B (t) = \lambda^{-(b + 2)} \left[ k_0 + \frac{k_1}{\lambda} + O (\lambda^{-2}) \right] ,
\tag{8}
$$
with $k_0$ and $k_1$ functions of the galaxy and of the angle between $g$ and
$\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ that do not depend on $t$. The remainder $B$ can be negative. When
$\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ is many $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ from $g$, $\Phi (t)$ is small and
$B$ is the larger term of $P$.

- `TRACE`: $k_1 = 0$. The terms of first order of the density of Eq. (4) around
  $\zeta = -1$ have the coefficient
  $-2 (\alpha_o - 1) - 2 (b + 2) + (b - 1) + 2 (\alpha_o + \alpha_1 + 2)$, which is zero
  for $b = 2 \alpha_1 + 1$, and $\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (u (r))$ has no term of first order
  in $1 - r$. The class sets $k_0 = \lambda_s^{b + 2} \, [P (t_s) - A (t_s)]$, with
  $\lambda_s$ the value of $\lambda$ at $t_s$.
- `TRACE_DET`: the same coefficient is $-(2 \alpha_o + b + 2)$, and $k_1 \ne 0$. The class
  sets $k_0$ and $k_1$ from $P - A$ at $t_s$ and at $1 - 10 \delta_s$.

The result is
$$
\ln P = \ln P (t_s) + \ln \left[ \frac{A (t)}{P (t_s)} +
\lambda^{-(b + 2)} \, \frac{k_0 + k_1 / \lambda}{P (t_s)} \right] ,
$$
with every term divided by $P (t_s)$ so that none leaves the double range. The difference
$1 - |g|^2$ is computed with the rounding errors of the two squares removed, and $\delta$
and $\lambda$ from it. A bracket that is not positive aborts as a non-finite $\ln P$.

## Interpolation in $g$

In a likelihood one galaxy is evaluated at many shears with the same
$\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ and $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$. With
[[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral:use-interp]] the class approximates
$\ln P (\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} \mid g)$ as a function of $g$ for each galaxy with
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_build]], described in
[Approximation on the Panels](../../../ncm/algebra/spectral_polar.qmd#approximation-on-the-panels),
and evaluates that approximation for $|g| \le g_\mathrm{max}$
([[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral:interp-g-max]]). For $|g| > g_\mathrm{max}$ it
computes the integral.

- Frame: rotated by the phase of $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$, so that
  $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} = e > 0$. In this frame $\ln P$ does not change under
  $g \to \bar{g}$, because the population is isotropic.
- Center: $g_c$, the shear that maps $\chi_I = 0$ to $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$:
  $g_c = e / (1 + \sqrt{1 - e^2})$ for `TRACE`, and 1 for $e \ge 1$; $g_c = e$ for
  `TRACE_DET`. The population density divided by $2 \pi |\chi_I|$ has its maximum, or its
  divergence for $\alpha_o < 1$, at $\chi_I = 0$, so $\ln P$ as a function of $g$ has its
  narrowest structure at $g_c$, of width $L_g = \sigma_\mathrm{noise} / 2$ for `TRACE` and
  $L_g = \sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ for `TRACE_DET`.
- Coordinates: $g = g_c + \rho \, e^{i \psi}$, with $\psi \in [0, \pi]$ by the reflection.
- Region: the rectangle in $(\rho, \psi)$ that contains the disk $|g| \le g_\mathrm{max}$:
  $[0, g_\mathrm{max} + g_c] \times [0, \pi]$ for $g_c < g_\mathrm{max}$, and otherwise
  $[g_c - g_\mathrm{max}, g_c + g_\mathrm{max}] \times [\pi - \arcsin (g_\mathrm{max} / g_c), \pi]$.
  It reaches $|g| = g_\mathrm{max} + 2 g_c < 3 g_\mathrm{max}$, so $g_\mathrm{max} < 1/3$
  keeps it inside $|g| < 1$, where $\ln P$ is smooth in $g$.
- Edges: the radial edges of [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_peak_edges]] for a peak at
  $\rho = 0$ of half width $L_g$ that are inside the region, with `min-radial-panels`
  equal to [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral:interp-min-radial-panels]] (default 2),
  and angular panels of $\pi / 2$ at most. The integrals use a separate
  [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]] with the default `min-radial-panels`, 2.
- Test: a panel is accepted when $\ln P$ changes by at most
  [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral:interp-abstol]] between its two grids. The
  values at the nodes are those of the integral at `reltol`.

The approximation of a galaxy is built at its first evaluation with
$|g| \le g_\mathrm{max}$ and kept with the galaxy. It is built again when
$\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$, $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$, the parameters of the population,
`reltol`, $g_\mathrm{max}$, the tolerance or `interp-min-radial-panels` differ from those it
was built for. A build
computes of the order of $10^3$ integrals, so the approximation reduces the cost when the
parameters of the population are fixed, and increases it when they change at every step
unless a galaxy is evaluated at more shears per step than the build computes.

## Measured Accuracy

The reference is the Arb tool `tests/tools/nc_galaxy_shape_marginal_arb.c`, which
certifies $\ln P$ with ball arithmetic. On its 20,062 certified points with
$(|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}| - 1) / \sigma_\mathrm{noise} \le 8$ and $|g| \ne 1$ (truncated
Gaussians of width 0.05 to 0.4, seven Beta populations, both conventions,
$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ from 0.005 to 1, $|g|$ from 0 to 3, real $g$), the largest
$|\ln P - \ln P_\mathrm{Arb}|$ per convention is:

| `reltol` | `TRACE` | `TRACE_DET` |
|---|---|---|
| $10^{-3}$ | $5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ | $5.0 \times 10^{-7}$ |
| $10^{-4}$ | $8.6 \times 10^{-8}$ | $2.2 \times 10^{-7}$ |
| $10^{-5}$ (default) | $6.9 \times 10^{-9}$ | $3.9 \times 10^{-9}$ |

No point failed. The tolerance bounds the change of the interpolant between grids, which
is why the differences are below it. The points with
$(|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}| - 1) / \sigma_\mathrm{noise} > 8$ are observations more than
eight noise standard deviations outside the disk; at the 3,057 certified ones the largest
difference at the default `reltol` is $2.5 \times 10^{-10}$, and at the 2,904 certified
points with $|g| = 1$ it is $2.9 \times 10^{-11}$. The unit test compares 23 certified
points, six of them at a complex $g$ not aligned with $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$, within
$10^{-7}$. The acceptance test `test_nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral_cert.c` compares all
26,023 certified points within $10^{-7}$; their table is a file of the data-file release,
written by `tests/tools/make_shape_marginal_arb_table.py`.

Next to $|g| = 1$ the reference is the same tool in its coordinates `--coords=uv`, for two
galaxies of the HSC catalog HWL16a-002 with the Beta population fitted to it,
$(\alpha, \beta) = (1.571, 1.654)$. The differences $\ln P - \ln P_\mathrm{Arb}$ at the
default `reltol` are:

| $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ | $\lvert \epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - g \rvert / \sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ | $1 - \lvert g \rvert$ | `TRACE` | `TRACE_DET` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0588 | 6.6 | $10^{-5}$ | $1.9 \times 10^{-13}$ | $-5.1 \times 10^{-12}$ |
| 0.0588 | 6.6 | $10^{-7}$ | $-3.6 \times 10^{-15}$ | $-2.1 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| 0.0403 | 22.3 | $10^{-6}$ | $-1.7 \times 10^{-10}$ | |
| 0.0403 | 22.3 | $10^{-8}$ | $-1.7 \times 10^{-10}$ | $-1.9 \times 10^{-9}$ |

In the first two rows $\Phi (t)$ is the larger term, and in the last two $B$ is. On 32
galaxies, 20 of that catalog and of HWL16a-064 and 12 with $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ of 0.01
and 0.03 and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ at 1 to 5 $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ from $g$, the class
returns a value at $|g| = 1 \pm 10^{-k}$ for $k = 6, \dots, 15$, in both conventions. The
values next to $|g| = 1$ were not measured for $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ below 0.01.

The interpolation in $g$ was measured on 150 galaxies of HWL16a-002 and HWL16a-064, 100 of
them with $\sigma_\mathrm{noise} < 0.1$, with $g_\mathrm{max} = 0.3$, against the integral
at `reltol` $10^{-8}$ on 200 random shears of the disk per galaxy, with
`interp-min-radial-panels` 2. No build failed. The integrals of a build and the largest
difference in $\ln P$ are:

| convention | population | `interp-abstol` | integrals, median / 90% / largest | largest difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRACE` | Beta, fitted | $10^{-4}$ | 927 / 1,858 / 2,372 | $4.4 \times 10^{-7}$ |
| `TRACE` | Beta, fitted | $10^{-5}$ (default) | 1,694 / 2,818 / 3,876 | $1.0 \times 10^{-8}$ |
| `TRACE` | Gaussian, 0.3 | $10^{-5}$ | 1,166 / 1,923 / 2,586 | $2.2 \times 10^{-9}$ |
| `TRACE_DET` | Beta, fitted | $10^{-5}$ | 523 / 1,502 / 3,010 | $6.5 \times 10^{-9}$ |
| `TRACE_DET` | Gaussian, 0.3 | $10^{-5}$ | 451 / 1,211 / 2,530 | $8.1 \times 10^{-9}$ |

One evaluation of the approximation takes 0.11 to 0.13 microseconds (median over the
galaxies) at the default tolerance, against 0.25 to 0.6 milliseconds for the integral at
$|g| \le 0.3$. For the Beta populations, `interp-min-radial-panels` 4 makes the evaluation
1.5 (`TRACE`) and 1.8 (`TRACE_DET`) times faster, for 13% and 11% more integrals in the
builds; with 1 the evaluation of `TRACE` Beta is 1.7 times slower, and the builds of the
four rows compute 4% to 16% fewer integrals.

## API Reference

See [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral]] for the class reference.
The function [[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral_eval_ln_direct]] computes $\ln P$
from a population and the values of one galaxy, and
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral_eval_panels]] also returns the panels the
integral was accepted on, in the polar coordinates of $\zeta$, with their angles in the
frame of $g$ and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$.
